Reading Skills

Reading skills for nurses — skimming, scanning, SQ3R and reading charts and labels.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe skimming and scanning
  • Explain the SQ3R method
  • State how to read charts, labels and orders safely

In simple words

Reading is understanding written text. Nurses read charts, doctor’s orders, medicine labels, reports and health education materials.

Different situations need different reading styles — skimming for the main idea, scanning for a fact, and careful reading for instructions.

Reading styles

Style Meaning Use
Skimming Read quickly for the main idea Getting the gist of a report
Scanning Look for a specific fact Finding a medicine dose on a label
Intensive Read carefully and fully Reading a doctor’s order or consent form
SQ3R Survey, Question, Read, Recite, Review Studying a textbook chapter

SQ3R method

  1. Survey — look at headings and pictures first.
  2. Question — turn headings into questions.
  3. Read — read to answer the questions.
  4. Recite — say what you remember.
  5. Review — go over it again later.

Reading charts and labels safely

  • Check the patient’s name on every chart and label.
  • Read medicine names, doses, routes and times carefully.
  • Check the date and time of entries.
  • If anything is unclear, ask — do not guess.

🔴 Read labels carefully

Read medicine names, doses, routes and times exactly. If anything is unclear, ask — never guess with medicines.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Doctor’s orders — read the full order before acting on it.
  • Medicine labels — check name, dose and expiry before giving.
  • Patient charts — read progress notes to know the patient’s condition.
  • Health teaching — read pamphlets aloud or explain them to patients who read poorly.
  • Reports — skim for the main point, then read details if needed.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Skimming is reading quickly for the main idea.
  2. Scanning is looking for one specific fact.
  3. Intensive reading is careful, full reading of instructions.
  4. SQ3R is Survey, Question, Read, Recite, Review.
  5. Check patient name, medicine name, dose, route and time on every label.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. If a label or order is unclear, ask — do not guess.
  2. Check the date and time of chart entries.
  3. Reading health education material helps patient teaching.

📌 Memory trick

SQ3R = “S-Q-3-R” — Survey, Question, Read, Recite, Review.

60-second revision

  • Styles: skimming, scanning, intensive, SQ3R.
  • Skim = main idea; scan = one fact; intensive = careful.
  • SQ3R: Survey, Question, Read, Recite, Review.
  • Labels: name, dose, route, time — check exactly.
  • Unclear? Ask, don’t guess.

Test yourself

Skimming means reading:

Answer: B. Skimming is reading quickly to get the main idea.

Scanning is used to:

Answer: B. Scanning means looking for one specific fact, like a dose on a label.

SQ3R stands for:

Answer: A. SQ3R is Survey, Question, Read, Recite, Review.

Before giving medicine, check the label for:

Answer: B. Check patient name, medicine name, dose, route and time before giving any medicine.

If a doctor’s order is unclear, the nurse should:

Answer: B. Never guess with medicines — ask and clarify before giving.
